# obsidian-mcp-rs

> Rust-based MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for Obsidian vaults. Lets AI assistants (Claude, Cursor, etc.) read, write, search, and manage notes inside Obsidian vaults over stdio transport.

## What it does

- Exposes 15 MCP tools for full note lifecycle management: create, read, edit, delete, move, search, tag, frontmatter, links, daily notes
- Supports multiple vaults simultaneously via CLI arguments
- Ships as a single static binary — no runtime required
- stdio by default; Streamable HTTP (`--http`) available via the optional `http` cargo feature
- Distributed as an npm package (`obsidian-mcp-rs`) with platform-specific binaries via optional dependencies, and on crates.io
- Installs itself into 14 AI-client configs and keeps itself updated from GitHub Releases

## Tools

- `read-note` — read a note; `view: "outline"` returns just its headings, block refs and frontmatter keys. Capped at 400 lines by default; page on with `offset`/`limit`
- `create-note` — create a new markdown note with content
- `edit-note` — append, prepend, replace, or find-and-replace — over the whole note, or scoped to one heading's section or one `^block-id`
- `delete-note` — move a note to the vault's `.trash/` (recoverable); `permanent: true` erases it
- `move-note` — move or rename a note, rewriting inbound `[[wikilinks]]` so they follow it. Omit `newFolder` to rename in place; pass `""` to move to the vault root
- `create-directory` — create a directory inside a vault
- `search-vault` — BM25-ranked search by content, filename, or tag (`tag:` prefix); paged via `limit`/`offset`. `regex: true` matches a pattern instead of words; `frontmatter: {"status": "active"}` keeps only notes carrying those fields (a list field matches when it contains the value), and works alone with an empty query
- `list-available-vaults` — list all configured vaults
- `wikilinks` — link graph: `backlinks`, `outgoing`, `broken`, `orphans`; paged via `limit`/`offset`
- `frontmatter` — read or write any YAML frontmatter key (`get`/`set`/`remove`), preserving the rest of the block
- `vault-info` — what's in the vault: `tags` (with counts), `recent`, `stats`; capped by `limit`
- `periodic` — daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/yearly notes (`get`/`create`/`list`), using Obsidian's own name, folder and template settings
- `add-tags` — add tags to frontmatter and/or content (`location`, `position`). Every file must exist, or nothing is changed
- `remove-tags` — remove tags from a note
- `rename-tag` — rename a tag across all notes in a vault

## Usage

```bash
npx -y obsidian-mcp-rs install claude-code /path/to/vault
```

`install` copies the server to a fixed per-user path and writes that absolute path into the client config. Node is not in the runtime path afterwards, and the configured path never changes. The installed copy keeps itself up to date: it checks for a new release at most once a day and replaces itself 48 hours after one ships. `install --no-auto-update` turns that off; `obsidian-mcp-rs update` takes a release immediately.

Configs are written for you rather than by hand — an entry that runs `npx` starts three processes per client, of which a client terminating "the server" kills only the first.

## Tech stack

- Language: Rust (stable)
- MCP library: rmcp 2.2 (stdio transport)
- CLI: clap
- Distributed via npm optional dependencies pattern
